I've had experience with people like this. They're called sociopaths. They specialize in finding altruistic and naive people and leveraging that empathy for maximum gain. They're much more common than you would believe and they blend in very well. Too well, actually. If you meet somebody and he presses all the right buttons, says all the right things where you just can't help but trust him, chances are it's a sociopath. This guy was in it for the short term gain, he got a can of fuel out of it. You might've not seen the last of him, I'd upgrade your home security.

There's also ones who are in it for long term gain. They will recognize that you are somebody who values empathy and honesty, and go for the long term gain. They won't steal from you outright, and they'll be the best friend somebody can be... until the moment arrives when they can leverage their relationship with you for maximum gain, they will stab you in the back and cut off all contact, even if you were 'best friends' for over 10 years. I know all this by personal experience, sadly. I myself have had a close encounter with the latter type of sociopath, though I wasn't the victim of his schemes.

Is there a way to recognize them, to avoid them entirely? No. All you can do is minimize your chances. High-intelligence sociopaths are completely unrecognizable to all but experts and other high-intelligence sociopaths. There's race though. Some races are more prone to sociopathic behavior. Also, real people make more mistakes. A sociopath only knows empathy by observation, so any emphatic behaviors will be just slightly off. There's some small signs, where the mask will come off just slightly. An off-hand joke about murdering cats, for example. I wish I could give you more information to help you recognize them, but it's up to you what you value more: taking chances and trusting people and risk being manipulated, or living with constant fear and paranoia and never trust anybody again. I chose the latter, and I think that was the wrong choice.
